questions.q: Name the three major supporting characters in "कहानी का पूर्ण" and state one distinct narrative function each serves in relation to the protagonist कहानी.
questions.a: Correct answer: (1) फेका — embodies practical labor and material reality, forcing कहानी to confront the physical necessity of "work" versus abstract storytelling; (2) हखर ठ — represents memory, tradition, and the weight of the past ("ईसक", "इप्सट"), making कहानी face its own history; (3) इस्क — embodies innocent curiosity and the future reader, asking the fundamental question "कहानी क्या होती है?" that exposes कहानी's existential void. A wrong answer that merely lists names without functions reveals the student confuses character identification with character analysis — a common board exam error where students write "फेका एक स्त्री है" instead of "फेका श्रम और यथार्थ का प्रतीक है जो कहानी को उसके अमूर्त भय से खींचकर ठोस धरातल पर लाती है".

questions.q: In the dialogue where फेका says "लकड़ी का काम है मेरा... यह रूह का सवाल नहीं, जिस्म का सवाल है" (page 79), explain how this line functions as a thematic counterpoint to कहानी's preoccupation with "अंत" (ending). Do not summarize the plot.
questions.a: Correct answer: फेका's line establishes a materialist worldview where survival ("जिस्म") precedes meaning ("रूह"), directly opposing कहानी's metaphysical anxiety about narrative closure. The contrast structures the story's central tension: कहानी seeks "अंत" as artistic completion, while फेका lives "अंत" as daily exhaustion. The word "काम" (work) recurs as both physical labor and narrative labor — फेका's woodwork mirrors कहानी's storytelling, but फेका accepts incompletion ("काम कभी पूरा नहीं होता") whereas कहानी fears it. A wrong answer that paraphrases the dialogue ("फेका लकड़ी का काम करती है") misses the thematic dialectic and will lose 2/3 marks in a board "explain the significance" question.

questions.q: Apply the "foil" concept to analyze how हखर ठ's "ईसक" (love/past) and इस्क's "इप्सट" (innocent questioning) function as opposing mirrors to कहानी's "अंत" (ending anxiety). Write a 4-step PEEL paragraph using one quote from each character.
questions.a:
**Step 1 (Point):** हखर ठ and इस्क serve as dual foils — one anchoring कहानी in the past, the other projecting it toward the future reader.  
**Step 2 (Evidence):** हखर ठ declares "ईसक ही जीवन है... इप्सट ही सत्य है" (p.81), while इस्क asks "कहानी क्या होती है? ...क्या वह कभी खत्म नहीं होती?" (p.82).  
**Step 3 (Explanation):** हखर ठ's "ईसक" represents accumulated memory that refuses closure — the past that won't stay past. इस्क's question represents the perpetual beginning — the reader who restarts the story. कहानी is trapped between them: haunted by what was (हखर ठ) and responsible for what will be read (इस्क).  
**Step 4 (Link):** Together they prove कहानी's "अंत" is impossible — not because stories don't end, but because every ending carries the past (हखर ठ) and births a new beginning (इस्क).  
A wrong answer that treats both characters as "similar because both talk to कहानी" flattens the structural opposition and fails the "analyze" command.

questions.q: Compare the narrative function of the minor character "विप्र" (the priest who appears briefly on page 83) with that of फेका. How does each represent a different institutional response to मानवीय पीड़ा (human suffering)? Support with textual details.
questions.a: Correct answer: फेका represents the *material/embodied* response — she shares physical labor ("लकड़ी का काम"), offers tangible presence ("मैं तुम्हारे साथ हूँ"), and accepts suffering as bodily reality ("जिस्म का सवाल"). विप्र represents the *ritual/abstract* response — he offers "मंत्र", "यज्ञ", "दान" as transactional solutions, treating suffering as karma to be appeased. The text contrasts them spatially: फेका sits *beside* कहानी ("पास बैठी"), विप्र stands *before* it ("सामने खड़ा"). फेका's "काम" is ongoing; विप्र's "कर्मकांड" is a closed transaction. A wrong answer that says "both try to help कहानी" misses the ideological critique — the story privileges फेका's solidarity over विप्र's ritual, reflecting Nirala's Marxist-humanist leanings. This distinction appears in CBSE "critical appreciation" questions.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "इस्क (the child) is the most important supporting character because it voices the reader's question." Defend or refute using evidence from the story's meta-fictional structure.
questions.a: Refute with nuance: इस्क *voices* the reader's question ("कहानी क्या होती है?"), but फेका *enacts* the reader's condition — living inside the story's material constraints. The meta-fictional structure makes कहानी both *author* and *character*; इस्क addresses कहानी as author ("तुम लिखते हो"), while फेका exists *within* the narrative world as co-laborer. Importance depends on the lens: for thematic exposition, इस्क is central; for existential grounding, फेका is indispensable. The story's closing image — फेका continuing her work ("काम चलता रहता है") while कहानी dissolves — proves the narrative privileges *continuity of labor* over *resolution of questioning*. A wrong answer that picks one character as "most important" without defining the criterion (thematic? structural? philosophical?) shows binary thinking — a JEE/NEET-style trap where "evaluate" demands conditional reasoning.

questions.q: Create a 4-line dialogue between two *new* supporting characters — a "पुस्तकालयाध्यक्ष" (librarian) and a "संपादक" (editor) — who encounter कहानी at the moment of its "अंत". Each must represent a distinct institutional attitude toward stories that contrasts with फेका, हखर ठ, and इस्क.
questions.a:
**Sample strong answer:**  
पुस्तकालयाध्यक्ष: "तुम्हारी शेल्फ नंबर तय है। अंतिम पृष्ठ पर स्टैम्प लगेगा — 'पूर्ण'।"  
संपादक: "बाजार तय करेगा तुम्हारा अंत। अगला संस्करण निकलने तक तुम 'अपूर्ण' रहोगे।"  
कहानी: "फिर मैं कौन हूँ — पाठ या वस्तु?"  
दोनों एक साथ: "तुम रिकॉर्ड हो। रिकॉर्ड का अंत नहीं, संग्रह होता है।"  

**Criteria for good answer:** (1) Each new character embodies a *distinct* institution (preservation vs. commodification), unlike the existing trio (labor, memory, innocence). (2) Dialogue advances the meta-fictional debate about "अंत". (3) कहानी's final question synthesizes the conflict. A poor answer makes the new characters sound like फेका/हखर ठ/इस्क variants (e.g., "पुस्तकालयाध्यक्ष: 'कहानी क्या होती है?'" — repeats इस्क's function).
